ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in triangle $ABC$, $AB=AC$, $\angle C=25^\circ$, point $D$ is on the extension line of segment $CA$, and $DA=AC$. What is the measure of $\angle ABD$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since AB = AC, and $\angle C = 25^\circ$, \\
hence $\angle ABC = 25^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle BAD = \angle C + \angle ABC = 50^\circ$, \\
since DA = AC, \\
hence AB = AD, \\
therefore $\angle ABD = \frac{1}{2} (180^\circ - \angle BAD) = \boxed{65^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point C is at the upper left, point B is at the upper right, and point D is at the lower right; line segments CB, BD, and CD form part of the boundary of the external triangle. Point A is located on the oblique line segment from C to D, so C, A, and D are collinear and A is between C and D; at the same time, line segment AB is drawn from A to B. Reasoning: It is known that AB=AC, so triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, with base BC, therefore ∠ABC=∠ACB. It is also known that ∠C=25°, that is, ∠ACB=25°, so ∠ABC=25°. Thus ∠BAC=180°-25°-25°=130°. Because D is on the extension of CA, ray AD and ray AC are in opposite directions, so ∠BAD and ∠BAC are supplementary, ∠BAD=180°-130°=50°. Also because DA=AC and AB=AC, AB=AD. Therefore triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, with vertex angle ∠BAD=50°, and the two base angles are equal, so ∠ABD=(180°-50°)/2=65°.
